system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: At 13:45:59 UTC, a 23.3-second HTTP flow from WS-MLOPEZ-01 to the explicit proxy recorded 51,000,324 origin bytes and 9,053 response bytes.
The flow record identifies the proxy as the destination but does not identify the ultimate web destination, request details, or originating process.
Firefox was launched by maria.lopez with metrics.eventpulse.com as its URL; a later proxy record shows a POST to that site's collection endpoint, which received status 301.
The Cisco AnyConnect VPN UI was launched by maria.lopez. The launch alone does not establish that a VPN connection was made.

known_telemetry_limitations: The provided evidence has a large-flow record but no matching proxy request record identifying its ultimate destination or HTTP method; the flow record itself contains only the proxy endpoint and byte counts (T009-00193).
The large-flow record does not associate the connection with a process or user, so endpoint process attribution is unavailable for that transfer (T009-00193).
The available network metadata does not reveal the content or purpose of the transferred bytes (T009-00193).
claims_not_established: Whether the bytes were sent onward to an external service, and if so, which service.
Whether the transfer was an upload of organizational data, what data it contained, or whether it was sensitive.
Which process initiated the transfer and whether maria.lopez intentionally initiated it.
Whether the AnyConnect client established a VPN connection.
Whether the transfer was authorized use of an approved service or malicious exfiltration.
additional_evidence_needed: Retrieve PROXY-HD-01 request and tunnel logs for the flow around 13:45:36–13:46:00 UTC, including destination host, URL, method, status, user, and byte counts.
Obtain endpoint network/process telemetry for the connection using source port 49308, including process image, command line, and user/session attribution.
Review endpoint artifacts and relevant file-access history around 13:45 UTC to identify any staged or accessed files associated with the transfer.
Check OneDrive and other approved-service audit records, plus available external-service or firewall logs, to determine whether the transfer completed and where it went.
Verify whether AnyConnect connected or attempted to connect during the review window.
